name: Called to serve
description: Five days on serving and leading the way Jesus did: humbly, faithfully, with your gifts.

days.title: Washing feet
days.note: Jesus takes the place of a servant.
days.devotional:
On His last night, Jesus kneels and washes His friends' feet, then tells them to do the same.

Greatness in His kingdom looks like serving.
days.prayer: Jesus, You knelt to serve. Make me willing to do the same.
questions: What is the 'foot-washing' task in your world?
Who could you serve quietly this week?

days.title: Gifts for others
days.note: Peter asks each person to use their gift for others.
days.devotional:
Each of us has received something from God to share, whether words or practical help.

Your gifts are meant to be given away.
days.prayer: Lord, show me the gifts You've given me, and how to use them for others.
questions: What gifts do others see in you?
Where could you use them this month?

days.title: One body
days.note: Paul pictures the church as a body.
days.devotional:
Every part matters, even the ones that seem less important. No one can say they are not needed.

You belong, and your part matters.
days.prayer: God, help me play my part, and value the part others play.
questions: Which part of the body do you feel you are?
Whose part do you tend to overlook?

days.title: Leading by serving
days.note: James and John ask for the best seats.
days.devotional:
Jesus turns their idea of leadership upside down: the one who wants to lead must serve, as He came to serve.

Leadership in His way is costly love.
days.prayer: Jesus, make me a leader who serves, like You.
questions: Where are you leading, at home, work or church?
What would serving look like there?

days.title: Faithful in little
days.note: Jesus speaks about faithfulness in small things.
days.devotional:
Jesus says that people who are trustworthy in small things are the ones trusted with bigger things. Small, unseen faithfulness matters to God.

Serving starts where you are.
days.prayer: Lord, help me be faithful in the small things You've given me today.
questions: What small responsibility could you do faithfully?
What would it mean to serve without being noticed?
